findings.claim: The webhook ordering rule accepts events with the same `event.created` timestamp, so an older `pending` event can overwrite `ready` despite the required same-second tie behavior.
findings.evidence: Line 119 applies when `event.created >= last_event_created`; line 183 expects a same-second event with another state not to apply and to trigger resync. The brief requires out-of-order webhooks never to move state backward.
findings.fix: Treat equal timestamps as ambiguous: do not apply the event state, set `resync_requested_at`, and test both delivery orders for same-second events.

findings.claim: The refund policy contradicts the brief's requirement that any refund row blocks payout by excluding failed or canceled Stripe refunds from `refund_seen_at` and the live-refund predicate.
findings.evidence: The brief's rule 3 and edge case require any refund row, full or partial and any status, to mean the request is never owed. Lines 28 and 189 instead say failed/canceled dashboard refunds are not refunds and leave the request owed; line 176 repeats the broader any-status expectation. Existing E02 filters are documented in `lib/payments/webhook.mjs` lines 12–15, so the payout spec needs an explicit additive rule that resolves this conflict rather than silently narrowing it.
findings.fix: Follow the brief: record the presence of any matched refund row regardless of status and exclude that payment from owed payouts; update OQ10 and the failed/canceled refund test expectation accordingly.
